question: After the timer-safety blocker is fixed, should OpenClaw accept a durable `gateway_restart_audit` table that stores bounded source, actor, device/IP, session fingerprint, and preflight metadata with 512-row retention?
rationale: The implementation adds a new durable local audit sink for operational metadata; code review can verify redaction mechanics, but the long-term payload and retention policy is a security-boundary choice for maintainers.

options.title: Accept bounded audit after timer fix
options.body: Land the durable audit direction once audit writes cannot delay restart timers and the existing redaction/retention tests stay green.

options.title: Narrow stored payload further
options.body: Keep the table but reduce persisted fields to source/reason/timing and identifiers only before merge.

options.title: Pause durable storage
options.body: Defer the SQLite audit sink and keep only non-durable logging until a broader audit policy is approved.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded audit after timer fix
recommendation.body: Land the durable audit direction once audit writes cannot delay restart timers and the existing redaction/retention tests stay green.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main work covers both restart SQLite state and shared state database behavior, which are the core ownership boundaries for this decision.
